title: Recursive Factorial
description:
A recursive function solves a problem by calling itself on a smaller one, with a base case to stop.
Define `long long fact(int n)`: fact(0) = 1, otherwise n * fact(n-1). Your function must call itself (no loops for the main work).

Input: one integer `n`.
Output: n! on one line.

title: Recursive Sum to N
description:
Define `int sumTo(int n)` returning 1 + 2 + ... + n recursively: sumTo(0) = 0, sumTo(n) = n + sumTo(n-1). Your function must call itself (no loops for the main work).

Input: one integer `n`.
Output: the sum.

title: Fibonacci Number
description:
The Fibonacci sequence starts 0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, ... where fib(0)=0, fib(1)=1, fib(n)=fib(n-1)+fib(n-2).
Define `int fib(int n)` recursively.

Input: one integer `n`.
Output: fib(n).

title: Recursive Power
description:
Define `long long power(int base, int exp)` where power(b, 0) = 1 and power(b, e) = b * power(b, e-1). Your function must call itself (no loops for the main work).

Input: `base` and `exp` separated by a space.
Output: base raised to exp.

title: Sum of Digits (Recursive)
description:
The last digit of n is `n % 10` and the rest is `n / 10`.
Define `int digitSum(int n)`: if n is 0 return 0, else last digit + digitSum(n / 10).

Input: one non-negative integer `n`.
Output: the sum of its digits.

title: Count Digits (Recursive)
description:
Define `int countDigits(int n)` that counts the digits of a non-negative number recursively. Numbers below 10 have exactly 1 digit (including 0); otherwise it is 1 + countDigits(n / 10).

Input: one integer `n`.
Output: its number of digits.

title: Countdown and Count Up
description:
Where you put a print relative to the recursive call changes the order!
Define `void countdown(int n)` which, for n >= 1, prints n on its own line, calls itself with n-1, and then prints n again on its own line after the call returns. For n = 0 it does nothing.
Hint: printing before the call gives the descending part, after the call the ascending part.

Input: one integer `n`.
Output: for n=3 the lines 3 2 1 1 2 3 (one number per line).

title: Recursive Array Sum
description:
Define `int arraySum(int arr[], int n)` that returns the sum of the first `n` elements recursively: the sum of 0 elements is 0, otherwise arr[n-1] + arraySum(arr, n-1).

Input: `n`, then `n` integers.
Output: their sum.

title: Recursive GCD
description:
Euclid's algorithm: gcd(a, 0) = a, otherwise gcd(a, b) = gcd(b, a % b).
Define `int gcd(int a, int b)` recursively.

Input: two non-negative integers `a` and `b`, not both zero.
Output: their greatest common divisor.
constraints: a and b are not both 0

title: Recursive String Length
description:
Without `strlen`, define `int length(const char *s)`: if `*s` is the terminator `'\0'` return 0, otherwise 1 + length(s + 1).

Input: one word without spaces.
Output: its length.

title: Reverse a Number
description:
Define `long long reverseNum(long long n, long long acc)` that builds the reversed number: if n is 0 return acc, else reverseNum(n / 10, acc * 10 + n % 10). Call it with acc = 0. Trailing zeros of n become leading zeros and vanish (120 -> 21).

Input: one non-negative integer `n`.
Output: the reversed number.

title: Palindrome Check
description:
A palindrome reads the same forwards and backwards. Define `int isPal(const char *s, int left, int right)`: if left >= right return 1; if s[left] != s[right] return 0; otherwise check the inside isPal(s, left+1, right-1).

Input: one word without spaces (case-sensitive).
Output: `Yes` if it is a palindrome, otherwise `No`.

title: Decimal to Binary
description:
Define `void toBinary(int n)` that prints the binary form of n with no newline: if n > 1, first call toBinary(n / 2); then print `n % 2`. The number 0 prints `0`.

Input: one non-negative integer `n`.
Output: its binary representation (main prints the newline).

title: Tower of Hanoi Move Count
description:
To move n disks you move n-1 disks aside, move the biggest one, then move n-1 disks back: moves(n) = 2 * moves(n-1) + 1, moves(0) = 0.
Define `long long hanoiMoves(int n)` recursively.

Input: one integer `n` (number of disks).
Output: the minimum number of moves.

title: Maximum of an Array (Recursive)
description:
Define `int maxOf(int arr[], int n)`: with 1 element it is that element; otherwise it is the larger of arr[n-1] and maxOf(arr, n-1).

Input: `n`, then `n` integers.
Output: the maximum value.

title: Recursive Binary Search
description:
Define `int search(int arr[], int lo, int hi, int target)` over a sorted ascending array: if lo > hi return -1; look at mid = (lo + hi) / 2; return mid if equal, otherwise search the left or right half recursively. Return the index of the target (all values are distinct).

Input: `n`, then `n` sorted distinct integers, then the `target`.
Output: the 0-based index of the target, or -1 if absent.
constraints: Elements are distinct and sorted ascending

title: Reverse a String
description:
Define `void rev(const char *s)` that prints the characters of s in reverse with no newline: if `*s` is the terminator do nothing; otherwise call rev(s + 1) first, then print `*s`.

Input: one word without spaces.
Output: the word reversed.

title: Tower of Hanoi Moves
description:
Print every move needed to solve Tower of Hanoi. Define `void hanoi(int n, char from, char to, char via)`: if n == 0 return; hanoi(n-1, from, via, to); print the move of disk n; hanoi(n-1, via, to, from).
Each move line has the form `Move disk D from X to Y`.

Input: one integer `n`; the disks start on peg `A`, must end on peg `C`, and `B` is the spare.
Output: one move per line in order.

title: Permutations of a String
description:
Print all arrangements of the letters of a word. The letters are distinct and given in increasing alphabetical order. Build each permutation position by position: for every letter not yet used, mark it used, place it, recurse to the next position, then unmark it (backtracking). Trying letters in order produces permutations in alphabetical order.
Suggested: `void permute(const char *s, int n, int pos, char *cur, int *used)`.

Input: one word of distinct lowercase letters in sorted order.
Output: every permutation, one per line, in alphabetical order.

title: Count Subsets with Given Sum
description:
Given `n` numbers, count the subsets (including the empty one, which has sum 0) whose elements add up to `target`. For each element you either include it or skip it. Define `int count(int arr[], int n, int idx, int remaining)`: at idx == n return 1 if remaining is 0 else 0; otherwise add count(include) and count(skip). Subsets are chosen by position, so equal values at different positions count separately.

Input: `n`, then `n` integers, then the `target`.
Output: the number of subsets.
